title: exists_reducedConstantLowerShriekReductionData
statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], f:X → Spec k a separated finite-type curve of dimension at most one [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting], X reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme], j:U → X an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and r a prime. Put R=ULift(Z/rZ) and let R_U/(r) denote the constant R-module sheaf with value R/(r) [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. There exist a scheme Y, a finite surjective morphism ν:Y → X [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism], a dense open V of X, a scheme U′, morphisms j′:U′ → Y and ν′:U′ → U, such that ν followed by f is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], ν restricted over V is an isomorphism, j′ is an open immersion, the square (j′,ν′,ν,j) is cartesian [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and j′_! R_U′/(r) [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] satisfies the eight assertions for Y → Spec k [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions]. Equivalently, ReducedConstantLowerShriekReductionData(f,j,r) [k1-reduced-constant-lower-shriek-reduction-data] holds.

proof.text: Choose the finite surjective smooth modification and dense isomorphism locus from reduced-curve normalization (Stacks 0A3Q, normalization paragraph), including the empty and zero-dimensional cases. Pull j back to this modification; base change preserves open immersions.

Split a smooth curve into finitely many open-and-closed irreducible components: smooth local rings are normal domains; Noetherianity makes the complement of a component closed. Apply the smooth constant Kummer or Artin--Schreier assertions, including the zero-dimensional cases. For each component the intersection with U is empty or dense, so dense-open localization yields its lower-shriek assertions. Finite pushforward and short-exact devissage assemble the finite direct sum. The smooth assertion packages use the smooth constant curve computations [thm-sc-main], preserving the unit's curve-calculation step.

proof_origin: Stacks 0A3Q, normalization paragraph, followed by Stacks 03SG, smooth lower-shriek proof: finite component decomposition, empty and zero-dimensional cases, characteristic-specific thm-sc-main calculations, dense-open localization, finite pushforward and devissage.
